newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower, trade thin after holiday.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower, trade thin after holiday.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed slightly lower following a two-day Christmas holiday, with dull activity anticipated through the next week.
Dealers said players have already closed their books for 1996. "We're not going to see anything until after the New Year," a trader said.
Local selling was cited throughout the session while speculative selling was noted on the close.
Volume remained light at an estimated 3,000 lots, with the most-active March contract settomg a tight 30-point range.
The front month ended 0.18 cent lower at 75.53 cents per pound, traded 75.85 to 75.50 cents. The back months finished 0.30 to 0.10 lower.
Support remained at 75.30 cents and resistance at 77.00 cents, basis the March contract.
The fundamentals were also unchanged as industry sources prepare for the annual Beltwide Cotton Conferences, which will be held in New Orleans Jan 6 to Jan 10.
